title: Finding Weaknesses, Not Victims
tagline: You have the version numbers. Now find out which doors are actually weak.
description: The service map is complete. Eight confirmed software versions across two Meridian Financial hosts. Now comes the step that separates professional assessment from guesswork: systematic vulnerability research. Learn what a vulnerability actually is, how CVE and CWE relate, how to read a CVSS score correctly, how to use the NVD to connect version strings to known weaknesses, and how to distinguish a potential CVE match from a confirmed finding using the CPR framework.
author: Cyber Learn Team
learningObjectives: Explain what vulnerability assessment is — and what distinguishes it from exploitation
Explain the difference between a vulnerability, an exposure, a weakness, and a misconfiguration
Define CVE, CWE, CVSS, and CPE — what each standard covers and how they relate
Use the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) to research known vulnerabilities for a confirmed software version
Interpret a CVSS base score — what it measures, what it does not, and how professionals use it for prioritisation
Explain the difference between a false positive and a false negative — and why both create professional risk
Apply the CPR framework to evaluate a CVE before treating it as a confirmed finding
skills: Searching the NVD systematically using software name and exact version string
Reading and interpreting CVE entries — affected versions, CVSS score, prerequisites, references
Applying the CPR framework to distinguish potential CVE matches from confirmed vulnerabilities
Documenting vulnerability research findings with evidence-based professional precision
